<reason>Both sides argued the motion as written with plausible causal reasoning and no fake sourcing, and both answered pressure questions with proper A1/A2 structure. But Side A did more decisive comparative work: the "currency" distinction (a payroll deduction is a structurable fraction of a paycheck; a lost retirement year is 100% of what the short-lived worker was owed) survived Side B's best counter that the roofer "pays under both policies." Side A's pressure questions were sharper and produced a usable concession — Side B admitted no employment-rate tripwire could mark the age hike a failure, which Side A converted into the memorable "faith, not policy" line that Side B's "the tax has the same hole" answer only partially defused (a payroll tax still collects from all employed workers regardless of older-worker hiring). Side A also caught the tension between Side B's "clean automatic rule" and yearly legislated exceptions, and reversed Side B's cost-laundering charge by showing the age hike routes spent-body workers into the very disability system Side B condemned as a shadow pension. Side B's structural ratio argument (years drawn vs. years paid, tax-base erosion) was genuinely strong and its exploitation of Side A's concession that legislated age rises are defensible landed in the closing, but it did less weighing on the equity clash that ultimately decided the debate. Both had a turn clipped for length — a shared minor execution cost. Narrow but real edge to Side A on clash engagement and framing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The roofer exchange: Side B's [B3.2]/[B5.2] pressed that the short-lived worker pays under both policies, so freezing the age just makes his wages finance retirements he won't live to collect. Side A's [A4.3] answer — that he pays in different currencies, a deductible fraction of money that can be shifted to high earners versus "one hundred percent of what pensions promised him" — was the most decisive moment, holding Side A's fairness core intact while giving the judge a clean reason to discount Side B's equivalence.</best_rebuttal>
